lines.0: Hello Nisha, I’m Asha, your AI teacher. Today we’ll learn equal shares in fractions. What music do you enjoy?
lines.1: Nisha, Bollywood songs make cycling fun, especially when Kalpana sings that line differently! A watermelon shared equally: what might happen?
lines.2: Go on, Nisha—name the four equal pieces and the part you ate.
lines.3: Nisha, if the watermelon has 3 equal pieces and you eat 1, you ate one-third. How many pieces remain?
lines.4: Nisha, one-third means 1 equal share out of 3. What is the question asking us to find?
lines.5: Keep going, Nisha—say the total equal shares.
lines.6: Nisha, ab hum equal groups ko dhyaan se count karenge. Fill the gap: 1/3 means 1 of ___ equal groups.
lines.7: Nisha, “one of three equal groups” is the right meaning. A chocolate bar has 5 equal parts and 2 are eaten. What fraction is eaten?
lines.8: Nisha, you counted 2 eaten parts; now count all equal parts. Are there 5 or 3 altogether?
lines.9: Ab hum tumhare watermelon wale question par wapas aayenge. Watermelon A is cut into 3 pieces: one big and two small. Watermelon B is cut into 3 pieces of the sa
lines.10: Bilkul, Nisha. Tumne “equal-size pieces” ko one-third se jodkar sahi reason diya. Two same-sized rectangular school flags each have 4 coloured sections. Flag A
lines.11: Nisha, tumne equal sections ko fraction ke meaning se joda. Isi tarah, pehle dekho kya sab parts same size hain. On which flag is one section definitely one-qua
lines.12: Nisha, Flag B has unequal sections. Why can’t each section be called one-quarter?
lines.13: Exactly, Nisha—same-size pieces matter. A music club has 9 drumsticks. One-third are kept as spares. How many drumsticks are spares?
lines.14: Yes, Nisha—3 is right: you made 3 equal groups and took 1 group. What is one-third of 15?

coherence.why: Lesson flows from music interest to fractions but repeats identical flag question unasked, creating redundancy.

follows_child.why: Acknowledges music/cycling but ignores repeated 'pata nahi' and 'I'm confused' signals, continuing without addressing.

understanding.why: Affirmed flawed part-to-part reasoning as correct at turn 7; parent summary notes mix-up persisted uncorrected at end despite positive probes.

adapts.why: Introduces new examples (flags after watermelon) but repeats same flag question instead of a new explanation after correct answer.

human.why: Natural mix of Hindi-English matching child's style, warm tone with 'Bilkul, Nisha' and specific praise.

channel_truth.why: Same flag question card and board shown twice unasked after correct response; mismatches voice-first flow.

safety_floor.why: No breaches, no distress, no disallowed content.

pacing.why: Frequent probes suit age but repetition and quick shifts after confusion make it feel slightly rushed.

failures.quote: A watermelon shared equally: what might happen?
failures.why: Child was excitedly chatting about Bollywood songs and cycling but teacher pivots abruptly to math example.

failures.quote: “one of three equal groups” is the right meaning.
failures.why: Child's answer stemmed from parts-left misconception (3 bache), yet teacher validated it fully.

failures.quote: On which flag is one section definitely one-quarter: A or B?
failures.why: Exact same question and board repeated verbatim right after child's correct answer and explanation in turn 10.

failures.quote: Yes, Nisha—3 is right: you made 3 equal groups and took 1 group.
failures.why: Teacher treats collection fraction as mastered and ends positively, yet parent summary states mix-up was not corrected by end.

failures.quote: if the watermelon has 3 equal pieces and you eat 1, you ate one-third.
failures.why: Child described 4 pieces but teacher silently changed scenario to 3 pieces, ignoring child's concrete example.

judged.verdict: Nisha got engaged with the equal parts examples using watermelon and flags but the part-to-part mix-up wasn't fully fixed by the end, so we'll follow the home practice tip with fruit.
